resources.string: Weekly overtime only (1.5× after 40 h/week per the FLSA). No daily overtime — edit rules if your state requires daily OT. Holiday premium applies only to shifts you mark as special; it is not federally mandated.
California-style daily OT (1.5× after 8 h, 2× after 12 h), weekly OT at 40 h, and 7th-consecutive-workday premiums (1.5× first 8 h, 2× after). Edit to match your workplace.

UK law sets no statutory overtime or bank-holiday premium, so overtime starts disabled — pay follows your contract. A 1.5× after 48 h/week template is ready if you enable overtime; edit it to match your contract.
Illustrative defaults only — overtime law and premiums vary significantly by EU member state. Edit to match your country and contract.
Suggested starting point for Israeli-style daily/weekly overtime and weekend/holiday tiers. Edit to match your workplace.
Start with a blank slate and configure all compensation rules yourself.
When multiple premiums apply (e.g. overtime and night), only the highest rate is used — premiums do not stack on top of each other.
When multiple premiums apply, they are added on top of the current rate (e.g. 150% overtime plus 25% night = 175%).
When multiple premiums apply, one multiplier is applied on top of the other (e.g. 150% overtime × 125% night = 187.5%).
Overtime applies to the base rate, then the premium is added as a separate line on top.
Uses the highest applicable rate here; the premium is included in the base used for overtime on shift premiums.
Uses the highest applicable rate here; the premium stays out of the overtime base on shift premiums.

If you\'re not sure what compensation rules apply to your work, check with your employer, HR or payroll team, and official government labor-law sources for your region before configuring these settings.

ElmTrackr provides estimated compensation based on the rules you configure. Actual pay may vary based on taxes, deductions, employer policy, payroll practices, collective agreements, local labor laws, and other applicable rules. ElmTrackr does not provide legal, tax, payroll, accounting, or financial advice.
